title: Submit & initialize
detail: Submission determines driver placement. Driver-side code creates or reuses the classic session and context.
data: Source data remains in storage. Startup is not a scan of the whole dataset.
evidence: Check deploy mode and the application identity; an attached notebook may already be initialized.

title: Acquire executors
detail: Resource allocation launches executor processes; executors register with the driver and become available for scheduling.
data: Data is still at its source. Adding compute does not imply all data is loaded into executor memory.
evidence: Check the Executors tab and resource requests. Dynamic allocation means executor count can change.

title: Describe & plan
detail: Expressions describe the query. Analysis resolves references; optimization and physical planning are demanded when needed, including by plan inspection or an action.
data: Metadata or schema work can occur. Planning and full result computation are distinct.
evidence: Compare analyzed, optimized, and physical plans with explain("extended"). This step is conceptual, not a claim that planning is eager.

title: Request & schedule
detail: An action requests a result. DAG scheduling creates stage task sets; task scheduling assigns attempts to available executor resources.
data: Tasks are ready to read or reuse the inputs they need. The cluster manager does not relay every task.
evidence: Follow the SQL execution to its jobs and stage tasks. Partition count is not the count of concurrent task slots.

title: Execute & exchange
owner: Executor tasks · adaptive planning on driver
detail: Tasks process partitions and produce shuffle output when the physical plan requires it. Downstream work fetches and combines it; AQE can adapt using runtime statistics.
data: Data travels through executor operators and, for a shuffle, local or remote blocks. Different keys can share a hash partition.
evidence: Inspect shuffle read/write, spills, task sizes, and the final adaptive plan. A broadcast exchange is a different operation.

title: Complete or recover
detail: Task status and metrics are tracked throughout execution. Recoverable failures can be retried; successful work returns results or commits output.
data: Display/collect results reach the driver. File output is normally written from executors; the driver coordinates completion.
evidence: Check completion and sink output. A finished query does not necessarily end the application.
